newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives discuss working with Labour - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives discuss working with Labour - paper.

text.p: A group of Conservative legislators is discussing how to cooperate with the opposition Labour party if it wins the next general election and the Conservatives elect a right-wing leader, the Observer newspaper said on Sunday.

The 30 or so moderate parliamentarians, horrified by a growing anti-Europe sentiment within their party, could help Labour leader Tony Blair push through pro-Europe legislation if he wins a narrow majority.

The newspaper said the movement could eventually lead to the creation of a new party, formalising Conservative splits over policy towards the European Union which have grown more serious under Prime Minister John Major.
A general election has to be held by May next year and a poll to choose the new leader of the Conservatives would follow about six months later.

The moderates no longer felt confident that their preferred candidate, Chancellor of the Exchequer (Finance minister) Kenneth Clarke, would be elected party leader and feared a hardline anti-European would be victorious instead.
The Observer said Blair knew about the existence of the Conservative group and might need its support to override possible opposition in his own ranks over Europe.

Blair himself told the Sunday Telegraph that he felt a number of moderate Conservative legislators would cooperate with a future Labour government if they saw it was trying "to get through a good and sensible programme of change".
